socfpga_i2c_ll.h

I2C low-level driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
SOCFPGA_I2C_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT

The standard active-polling limit in microseconds for low-level synchronous FIFO and status operations before yielding a hardware timeout fault.

SOCFPGA_I2C_FALLBACK_SPINS_PER_US

Loop bound used in place of a microsecond deadline when CNTFRQ_EL0 reads zero, which happens in host unit builds and during pre-PLL bring-up.

I2C speed modes

Speed class chosen from the requested bus rate. The SCL counts and the controller speed field are set from this class.

SOCFPGA_I2C_SPEED_STANDARD

Standard mode, 100 kbit/s. Chosen when the bus rate is at most 100000 Hz.

SOCFPGA_I2C_SPEED_FAST

Fast mode, 400 kbit/s. Chosen when the bus rate is above 100000 Hz and at most 400000 Hz.

SOCFPGA_I2C_SPEED_FASTPLUS

Fast-mode Plus, 1000 kbit/s. Chosen when the bus rate is above 400000 Hz.

socfpga_i2c_ll_probe_controller
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_probe_controller(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
*
version
)

Reads IC_COMP_TYPE to confirm a DesignWare I2C controller is present, clocked and out of reset at the supplied base address. This distinguishes an absent or unclocked instance from a healthy controller whose bus has no target on it.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

version
uint32_t*

Optional output for the IC_COMP_VERSION value; may be NULL.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL for a null base address, or -ENODEV when the component signature does not match.

socfpga_i2c_ll_configure_master
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_configure_master(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint16_t 
target_address,
uint32_t 
speed_mode,
bool 
ten_bit_address,
bool 
restart_enable
)

Configures the foundational operational mode of the I2C IP block. This writes to the IC_CON (Control) and IC_TAR (Target Address) registers to set the bus speed, addressing format, and RESTART capabilities. The controller must be disabled prior to calling this function.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

target_address
uint16_t

The 7-bit or 10-bit address of the slave device to communicate with.

speed_mode
uint32_t

The SCL speed mode (1=Standard, 2=Fast, 3=Fast Plus).

ten_bit_address
bool

true to configure the master for 10-bit addressing mode.

restart_enable
bool

true to allow the hardware to generate repeated START conditions.

Returns

0 on success.

socfpga_i2c_ll_set_scl_count
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_set_scl_count(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
speed_mode,
uint16_t 
high_count,
uint16_t 
low_count
)

Manually overrides the calculated hardware clock divisors for the Serial Clock (SCL) line. This writes directly to the IC_SS_SCL_HCNT/LCNT or IC_FS_SCL_HCNT/LCNT registers depending on the active speed mode.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

speed_mode
uint32_t

The SCL speed mode currently targeted for adjustment.

high_count
uint16_t

The number of `ic_clk` cycles the SCL line will remain high.

low_count
uint16_t

The number of `ic_clk` cycles the SCL line will remain low.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL for a null base address or a zero count.

socfpga_i2c_ll_set_timing
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_set_timing(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
ic_clk_hz,
uint32_t 
bus_hz,
uint32_t 
*
speed_mode
)

Derives and programs the SCL high/low counts and the SDA hold time for the requested bus frequency from the controller input clock. Without this the counts keep their synthesis reset values and the resulting SCL frequency is undefined. IC_CON is not touched; the resolved speed mode is reported through speed_mode so the caller can program IC_CON.SPEED to match.

The count equations match the U-Boot and Linux DesignWare drivers: SCL high = (HCNT + 3) * ic_clk period + fall time SCL low  = (LCNT + 1) * ic_clk period - fall time + rise time

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

ic_clk_hz
uint32_t

The controller input clock frequency in hertz.

bus_hz
uint32_t

The requested SCL frequency in hertz.

speed_mode
uint32_t*

Output for the resulting SOCFPGA_I2C_SPEED_STANDARD class speed mode; may be NULL.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL when a clock or frequency is zero, or -ERANGE when the input clock is too slow to meet the timing minimums of the requested speed.

socfpga_i2c_ll_set_target_address
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_set_target_address(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint16_t 
target_address,
bool 
ten_bit_address,
uint32_t 
timeout
)

Retargets the master at a different device without re-initializing the controller. IC_TAR is only writable while the controller is disabled, so this disables it, updates IC_TAR and IC_CON, and re-enables it.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

target_address
uint16_t

The 7-bit or 10-bit address of the device to address next.

ten_bit_address
bool

true when target_address is a 10-bit address.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds for the disable/enable handshake.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL for a bad address, or -ETIMEDOUT on a stuck controller.

socfpga_i2c_ll_probe_address
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_probe_address(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
timeout,
uint32_t 
*
abort_source
)

Performs a single-byte read against the currently programmed target address purely to observe whether the device acknowledges, which is the bus scan primitive behind i2cdetect. The byte read is discarded.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds for the probe transaction.

abort_source
uint32_t*

Optional output for IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE on failure; may be NULL.

Returns

0 when the target acknowledges; -ENXIO when it does not; -ETIMEDOUT when the bus does not respond at all.

socfpga_i2c_ll_recover_bus
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_recover_bus(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
timeout
)

Attempts to return a wedged bus to idle. An in-flight transfer is cancelled with IC_ENABLE.ABORT, then the controller is cycled through disable and enable to flush both FIFOs and re-arm the master state machine.

This recovers the controller, not the wire. A target holding SDA low needs SCL pulsed through pinmuxed GPIO, which this driver does not own.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds for each recovery step.

Returns

0 when the bus returns to idle; -ETIMEDOUT when it stays busy.

socfpga_i2c_ll_write_sync
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_write_sync(
uint32_t 
base_address,
const 
uint8_t 
*
buffer,
size_t 
length,
uint32_t 
timeout,
uint32_t 
*
abort_source
)

Orchestrates a low-level, polling-based write sequence. This function pushes data bytes into the Transmit (TX) FIFO by writing directly to the IC_DATA_CMD register, spin-polling the IC_STATUS register to avoid FIFO overflow, and waiting for the TX FIFO to fully drain.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

buffer
const uint8_t*

Pointer to the payload buffer.

length
size_t

Number of bytes to push to the TX FIFO.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds to wait for FIFO space or completion.

abort_source
uint32_t*

Optional output for IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE on failure; may be NULL. The register is cleared as it is read, so this is the only chance to capture it.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT if the bus hangs, or -EIO if a hardware NACK occurs.

socfpga_i2c_ll_read_sync
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_read_sync(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint8_t 
*
buffer,
size_t 
length,
uint32_t 
timeout,
uint32_t 
*
abort_source
)

Orchestrates a low-level, polling-based read sequence. This function issues read requests by writing the CMD bit to the IC_DATA_CMD register. It then polls the IC_STATUS register to ensure the Receive (RX) FIFO is not empty before extracting the incoming bytes.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

buffer
uint8_t*

Pointer to the destination buffer.

length
size_t

Number of bytes to read from the target.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds to wait for the RX FIFO to populate.

abort_source
uint32_t*

Optional output for IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE on failure; may be NULL.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT if the target fails to return the requested bytes.

socfpga_i2c_ll_write_then_read_sync
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_write_then_read_sync(
uint32_t 
base_address,
const 
uint8_t 
*
tx_buffer,
size_t 
tx_length,
uint8_t 
*
rx_buffer,
size_t 
rx_length,
uint32_t 
timeout,
uint32_t 
*
abort_source
)

Executes a raw, combined format transaction utilizing a hardware RESTART condition.

This function packs the TX phase into the IC_DATA_CMD register, sets the RESTART bit on the final TX byte, and seamlessly transitions into pushing read requests (CMD bit set) for the RX phase. This guarantees the bus is not relinquished between the write and read operations.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

tx_buffer
const uint8_t*

Pointer to the data to transmit (e.g., register offset).

tx_length
size_t

Number of bytes to transmit before the RESTART.

rx_buffer
uint8_t*

Pointer to the destination buffer for the incoming data.

rx_length
size_t

Number of bytes to read after the RESTART.

timeout
uint32_t

Maximum time in microseconds for the combined transaction.

abort_source
uint32_t*

Optional output for IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE on failure; may be NULL.

Returns

0 on success; -ETIMEDOUT or -EIO on bus failure.

socfpga_i2c_ll_get_intr_status
uint32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_get_intr_status(
uint32_t 
base_address
)

Samples the IC_INTR_STAT register. This identifies which internal hardware events (e.g., TX_ABRT, RX_FULL, TX_EMPTY) are currently active and unmasked, signaling the need for software intervention.

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

Returns

socfpga_i2c_ll_get_tx_abort_source
uint32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_get_tx_abort_source(
uint32_t 
base_address
)

Reads the IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE register. If an operation fails (indicated by the TX_ABRT interrupt), this register provides the specific root cause, such as a 7-bit Address NACK, Data NACK, or Arbitration Lost.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

Returns

The raw 32-bit diagnostic value containing the abort flags.

socfpga_i2c_ll_abort_to_errno
int32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_abort_to_errno(
uint32_t 
abort_source
)

Translates an IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE bitmap into the errno that describes it, so every caller reports an absent target, a data NACK, lost arbitration and a protocol error the same way.

Parameters
abort_source
uint32_t

A value read from IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE.

Returns

-ENXIO for an address NACK, -EIO for a data NACK, -EAGAIN for lost arbitration, or -EPROTO for a request the current IC_CON forbids.

socfpga_i2c_ll_mask_all_interrupts
void socfpga_i2c_ll_mask_all_interrupts(
uint32_t 
base_address
)

Writes 0x0 to the IC_INTR_MASK register, effectively silencing all hardware interrupt generation from this I2C instance to the system GIC.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

Returns

None.

socfpga_i2c_ll_clear_interrupts
void socfpga_i2c_ll_clear_interrupts(
uint32_t 
base_address
)

Performs a dummy read of the IC_CLR_INTR register. By hardware design, reading this specific register automatically clears all combined and individual software- clearable interrupts across the IP block.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

Returns

None.

socfpga_i2c_ll_read_reg
uint32_t socfpga_i2c_ll_read_reg(
uint32_t 
base_address,
uint32_t 
offset
)

Performs a direct 32-bit Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) read from an arbitrary register offset within the I2C instance.

Parameters
base_address
uint32_t

The physical MMIO base address of the target I2C instance.

offset
uint32_t

The exact 32-bit aligned register offset to read.

Returns

The raw 32-bit hardware value.

Notes

This is an intentionally thin, lockless helper. It expects the caller to validate the address and offset.
